# **Architecture for a Centralized Context and Corroboration Engine in Browser-Based Web Auditing**

To eliminate false-positive score collapses on enterprise websites, a browser auditing extension must decouple raw rule detection from score penalty assessment through a five-stage pipeline: RawModuleData \-\> FindingBuilder \-\> ContextCorroborator \-\> ScoringEngine \-\> UserReport. In this architecture, individual rule modules remain simple and deterministic, while a centralized middleware hosted inside the Manifest V3 (MV3) background service worker cross-validates every candidate finding against live Core Web Vitals, DOM surface capabilities, normalized URL semantics, asset mutability boundaries, and cross-origin visibility constraints.  
Instead of feeding binary pass/fail verdicts into rigid category caps, the ContextCorroborator classifies each raw finding into one of four reality states—TRUE\_DEFECT, ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN, OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT, or SYNTHETIC\_NOISE—and assigns a continuous reality multiplier (![][image1]). The ScoringEngine replaces global caps with a blast-radius-weighted violation density model while excluding unobservable checks from the score denominator into a separate Telemetry Coverage Index (TCI), ensuring opaque network or browser boundaries reduce reported visibility rather than artificially inflating defect penalties.  
Two caveats constrain this architecture. First, browser extensions operating without the intrusive chrome.debugger permission face hard platform blind spots—including inaccessible HTTP response bodies, no-cors opaque responses, Timing-Allow-Origin masking, and cross-origin CSSOM limits—that can only be surfaced honestly as observability gaps rather than inferred as failures1. Second, the mathematical scoring parameters in Section 3 are calibrated from simulation models across representative storefront and authentication edge cases rather than an external live-corpus benchmark, and should be validated against your own site telemetry before locking production thresholds5.

## **1\. Taxonomy of Reality and Finding Classification Matrix**

Naive scanners generate misleading score collapses on e-commerce platforms, news portals, and single-page applications because they collapse four operationally distinct conditions into a single Violation state. Static DOM and header checks cannot inherently discern whether a spec discrepancy harms users, implements an intentional multi-origin enterprise boundary, reflects an extension observability limit, or represents a heuristic refuted by runtime browser execution. Separating these states adapts established triage boundaries from axe-core, which isolates uncertain incomplete (cantTell) outcomes from verified violations6; Google Lighthouse, which excludes notApplicable and informative audits via scoreDisplayMode9; and OWASP ZAP, which pairs Alert Thresholds with Confidence levels in passive HTTP checks11.

| Reality State | Definition and Decision Criteria | Enterprise False-Positive Examples | Scoring Treatment and Multiplier | User Report Presentation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| TRUE\_DEFECT | Verified defect with demonstrable user-experience, accessibility, SEO indexation, or security impact on this exact page. | Missing accessible names on checkout submit controls; missing SRI on a pinned public CDN library; missing CSP/HSTS on a credential-capturing login page. | Included in category denominator; standard defects use ![][image2], with intermediate values in ![][image3] available for partially mitigated findings5. | Actionable Defect badge showing severity, affected blast radius, and verified reproduction evidence. |
| ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN | Intentional enterprise engineering or trust-boundary trade-off rather than developer oversight. | Canonical tag consolidating campaign tracking parameters (utm\_\*, gclid); missing strict CSP/HSTS on a public read-only catalog where checkout isolates to a dedicated subdomain; missing SRI on dynamic fraud scripts such as Stripe.js13. | Excluded from penalty denominator (treated equivalently to notApplicable)9; ![][image4]. | Informational / Verified Pattern badge explaining the detected enterprise pattern and compensating controls. |
| OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT | Condition outside the browser extension's visibility boundary due to same-origin limits, MV3 constraints, or upstream infrastructure. | Cross-origin CSSOM restrictions; no-cors opaque responses hiding status/headers/body; missing Timing-Allow-Origin zeroing resource sub-timings; edge WAF header rewriting; search-engine-selected canonical divergence1. | Excluded from scoring denominator; reduces the separate Telemetry Coverage Index (TCI) proportionally to rule weight5. | Unverified / Masked badge naming the exact visibility boundary (e.g., no-cors opacity, missing TAO, or MV3 body limit) without penalizing score. |
| SYNTHETIC\_NOISE | Technically true against an isolated heuristic or static rule, but empirically nullified by live runtime telemetry. | Render-blocking warning contradicted by fast live FCP (\<700 ms) and LCP (\<2.1 s); DOM depth or script-count warning alongside zero long animation frames (\>50 ms) and passing Core Web Vitals16. | Included in denominator with heavy confidence decay (e.g., ![][image5]), preserving near-full score credit5. | Suppressed / Low-Impact Note under diagnostics, displaying the overriding runtime telemetry proof. |

State transitions in the ContextCorroborator follow strict precedence so overlapping signals never conflict: OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT takes priority whenever required collector inputs were blocked by browser security boundaries or absent permissions; ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN overrides defect emission when structural evidence proves intentional isolation or asset mutability; SYNTHETIC\_NOISE triggers when live runtime performance or user-impact signals refute a static heuristic; and TRUE\_DEFECT remains only when a candidate survives observability verification and contextual corroboration. Separating OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT from ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN is essential for audit transparency: a 100 category score paired with a 93.2% Telemetry Coverage Index communicates high quality within known blind spots rather than false certainty5.

## **2\. Multi-Signal Corroboration Engine**

Rather than embedding fragile domain allowlists inside individual rules, the ContextCorroborator cross-validates independent telemetry graphs gathered across page load and interaction. Each collector supplies orthogonal evidence—paint and animation frame timelines, DOM interactive capability inventories, HTTP response headers, and normalized URL components—allowing one subsystem to confirm or falsify the assumptions of another.

### **Performance Corroboration Against Live Core Web Vitals**

Static heuristics and network simulators frequently misclassify modern module and preload architectures because proxy metrics (DOM depth, script counts, initial request priority) do not uniformly map to real paint delays. In a documented Lighthouse GitHub issue (\#17163), investigators demonstrated that Lantern kept a type="module" Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon in the render-blocking graph because it defaulted to High initial priority and lacked a trace EvaluateScript URL association—inflating simulated FCP to 1,951.9 ms on a captured artifact set whose observed FCP was 225 ms and whose Chrome DevTools Protocol classification was NonBlocking, while another commenter on Lighthouse 13.5.0 reported pages painting at \~0.8–1.4 s observed versus 4.8–5.3 s simulated FCP16.  
Separate Lighthouse issue threads also illustrate the practical nuance around CSS warnings: one thread notes that preload hints combined with slightly slower synthetic conditions can intermittently flip stylesheets into the render-blocking audit across consecutive tests on unchanged code19, while another exposes an active engineering debate—a contributor argued that flagging a single required CSS file nudges developers toward deferral strategies that trigger flashes of unstyled content and layout shifts, whereas Lighthouse maintainers countered that inlining critical CSS still saves cold-load connection overhead for stylesheets under \~100 KB and clarified that the render-blocking audit does not directly reduce the Lighthouse Performance score19.  
To resolve synthetic noise without masking genuine regressions, the corroborator evaluates static performance flags against Google's Core Web Vitals thresholds—Largest Contentful Paint (LCP ≤ 2.5 s), Interaction to Next Paint (INP ≤ 200 ms), and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS ≤ 0.1)18—alongside live PerformanceResourceTiming.renderBlockingStatus ("blocking" or "non-blocking") and Long Animation Frames (PerformanceLongAnimationFrameTiming, or LoAF)1. Because renderBlockingStatus currently has limited cross-browser availability (75.68% global support according to Can I Use, supported in Chrome 107+)21 and LoAF remains an experimental API that omits script attribution for cross-origin \<iframe\>s, workers, and extension code22, missing attribution data is treated conservatively rather than assumed benign. Following Datadog RUM's production collection safeguards, live FCP/LCP timings from pages opened in background tabs must be discarded, and missing INP values on zero-interaction loads must never trigger penalties23.

> 1. **Render-Blocking Suppression Gate**: When a static DOM or network rule flags a \<script\> or \<link rel="stylesheet"\> as render-blocking, check live Navigation/Paint Timing and Resource Timing. If observed FCP \< 700 ms and LCP \< 2.1 s (well within the 2.5 s CWV target18), or if PerformanceResourceTiming.renderBlockingStatus explicitly reports "non-blocking"1, reclassify the finding as SYNTHETIC\_NOISE with confidence multiplier ![][image5]5. Retain TRUE\_DEFECT only when FCP ≥ 700 ms or LCP \> 2.1 s and the asset blocks initial paint.  
> 2. **Single-Stylesheet Nuance Gate**: When exactly one same-origin stylesheet reports "blocking" while FCP \< 700 ms and CLS ≤ 0.11, downgrade the warning to SYNTHETIC\_NOISE rather than recommending asynchronous deferral that risks FOUC and CLS degradation19, optionally retaining a low-priority diagnostic note on inlining if cold-load overhead exceeds thresholds20.  
> 3. **DOM Depth and Script-Count LoAF Gate**: When heuristic rules flag excessive DOM size or high script counts, inspect long-animation-frame entries (duration \> 50 ms) and PerformanceScriptTiming fields17. If INP ≤ 200 ms18 and no LoAF entries exhibit blockingDuration \> 50 ms or elevated forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration17, reclassify to SYNTHETIC\_NOISE; if LoAF attribution isolates a specific sourceURL driving \>50 ms frame delays or style thrashing, escalate that script to TRUE\_DEFECT17.  
> 4. **Cross-Origin Timing Observability Check**: Before flagging third-party resource anomalies (connectEnd \- connectStart, secureConnectionStart, or serverTiming), inspect whether those properties return 0 due to an absent Timing-Allow-Origin header or cross-origin iframe fallback behavior1. When TAO is missing, reclassify sub-phase timing gaps as OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT rather than reporting 0 ms anomalies.

### **Security Corroboration via Surface Capability and Domain Isolation**

Static HTTP security scanners create high false-positive volume on enterprise e-commerce and media architectures because they audit public read-only catalog pages identically to authenticated checkout endpoints. Enterprise teams routinely segregate trust zones so high-traffic public storefronts remain edge-cacheable while credential entry and payment processing isolate onto dedicated origins (login.\*, checkout.\*). OWASP ZAP's passive scanning engine applies similar contextual gating—for example, skipping missing CSP alerts on redirects unless the Alert Threshold is Low, and downgrading Cache-Control alerts to Info because caching is often valid11.  
Your ContextCorroborator builds a **Page Surface Capability Profile** from DOM and passive network collectors prior to scoring header or cookie rules. This profile inspects five concrete signals: \<input type="password"\> or WebAuthn triggers, mounted payment SDK widgets or payment iframes28, authenticated session cookies (distinguished from anonymous analytics/preference cookies), active state-changing \<form method="POST"\> or credentialed fetch/XHR mutations, and sensitive PII autocomplete fields.  
On a page classified as READ\_ONLY\_PUBLIC—zero password or payment inputs, no authenticated session cookies, and no state-changing POST forms—missing strict CSP or Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) headers should not collapse security scores. If navigation links or form targets confirm an isolated checkout/authentication subdomain, missing strict CSP on the read-only catalog reclassifies as ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN (advisory hardening); without detected isolation, it remains a low-impact advisory (![][image6]). Conversely, whenever credential inputs, payment frames, or session cookies exist (AUTH\_OR\_PAYMENT\_SURFACE), missing HSTS or unsafe CSP configurations—such as default-src missing or allowing 'unsafe-inline', or policies permitting 'unsafe-hashes'11—immediately assert TRUE\_DEFECT with ![][image2].  
Two additional corroborations resolve common enterprise header and cookie false positives. First, cookie audits checking HttpOnly must differentiate authentication cookies from client-side anti-fraud telemetry cookies: as noted in Stripe's stripe-js GitHub repository discussions (issue \#906 / PR \#910), \_\_stripe\_mid and \_\_stripe\_sid hold no authentication credentials and omit HttpOnly by design because Stripe.js must read and write them via JavaScript for fraud-signal correlation13. Correlating cookie domain/names with an active Stripe payment integration allows safe reclassification to ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN. Second, when Strict-Transport-Security is absent from an HTTPS response, a passive client script cannot immediately tell whether Chrome enforces HTTPS via its embedded HSTS Preload List (used by Chrome, Firefox, and Safari even on first visit) or whether an edge WAF strips/rewrites origin headers29. Querying a bundled HSTS preload index resolves preloaded domains to ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN, while unverified edge-WAF masking where http\:// upgrade behavior cannot be observed maps to OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT.

### **Semantic SEO Canonical Evaluation**

Exact string matching between link\[rel="canonical"\] and window.location.href breaks on nearly every paid marketing, affiliate, and social landing page. Google Lighthouse's documentation states that consolidating external query parameters onto a preferred URL is a core purpose of canonical tags, and Lighthouse's canonical.js audit fails only on structural defects: multiple canonicals, invalid URLs, cross-domain canonicals, region/language (hreflang) mismatches, or lower-level paths pointing to the site root14.  
The SEO corroborator replaces naive string equality with five sequential normalization and superset checks:

> 1. **URL Normalization**: Lowercase scheme and host, remove default ports, strip \#fragment identifiers31, and normalize trailing slashes.  
> 2. **Structural Invariant Checks**: Verify at most one canonical declaration exists across HTML \<link rel="canonical"\> and HTTP Link: ...; rel=canonical headers, and validate URL syntax14.  
> 3. **Origin and Path Equivalence**: Compare normalized origin \+ pathname. Cross-domain targets or subpaths pointing to / remain TRUE\_DEFECT unless paired with explicit AMP/mobile alternate relations14.  
> 4. **Query Parameter Superset Analysis**: Decompose query dictionaries ![][image7] and ![][image8]. If ![][image9] and every dropped parameter in ![][image10] belongs to a curated tracking/attribution taxonomy (utm\_\*, gclid, fbclid, msclkid, spm, ref, mc\_cid), reclassify the mismatch as ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN (valid parameter consolidation). If substantive catalog/state keys (id, sku, page, q, category) are dropped, or if ![][image8] introduces new keys absent from ![][image7], preserve TRUE\_DEFECT.  
> 5. **Indexation Boundary Annotation**: Distinguish the *user-declared* canonical observable in the browser from the *Google-selected* canonical reported in Google Search Console, explicitly scoping search-engine selection as an OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT14.

### **Subresource Integrity Asset Mutability Filtering**

Requiring Subresource Integrity (integrity="sha384-...") on every third-party \<script\> guarantees false positives because SRI is structurally incompatible with dynamic vendor scripts13. SRI validates cryptographic digests (sha256/sha384/sha512) before execution35 and requires deterministic bytes fetched with CORS (crossorigin="anonymous" rather than opaque no-cors mode)2. In stripe-js GitHub issue \#167, a Stripe contributor explicitly confirmed that https\://js.stripe.com/v3 does not support SRI because Stripe regularly deploys live updates to maintain PCI regulatory coverage and fraud defenses13. Tag managers (tagmanager.google.com/gtm.js), analytics (google-analytics.com/analytics.js), and ad pixels (connect.facebook.net/en\_US/fbevents.js) similarly update upstream without versioned hashes34. Note also that the experimental CSP require-sri-for directive is obsolete and removed from modern browsers28, while industry discussion under PCI DSS 4.0.1 Requirements 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 favors script inventories, CSP allowlisting, and continuous runtime tamper/hash monitoring when SRI is unavailable34.

| Third-Party Asset Class | Detection Signature in Corroborator | SRI Feasibility and Reality Classification | Recommended Remediation / Control Output |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Pinned Public Library CDN | Public library CDN (cdnjs, cdn.jsdelivr.net37, unpkg) loading an immutable versioned path (e.g., /3.7.1/, @1.4.2). | SRI fully feasible. Missing integrity or crossorigin="anonymous" classified as TRUE\_DEFECT (![][image2]). | Add integrity="sha384-..." and crossorigin="anonymous"35. |
| Rolling / Unpinned Public CDN | Library CDN using floating paths (/latest/, @main, unversioned majors) or cache-busting query strings. | Upstream updates break static hashes. Classified as TRUE\_DEFECT (unpinned dependency defect). | Pin an immutable versioned URL before adding SRI, or bundle/self-host locally28. |
| Dynamic SaaS, Payment & Tag Scripts | Rolling vendor endpoints requiring continuous live updates (js.stripe.com/v3, tagmanager.google.com/gtm.js, google-analytics.com/analytics.js, fbevents.js)13. | SRI architecturally impossible without breaking vendor security/fraud updates13. Classified as ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN (![][image4]). | Recommend CSP origin allowlisting, documented script inventory, and continuous behavioral/hash monitoring per PCI DSS 4.0.1 (6.4.3/11.6.1)36; track emerging Signature-based Integrity38. |
| no-cors / Opaque Cross-Origin Assets | Cross-origin fetch or resource without CORS yielding an opaque response (status 0, headers and body unreadable by JavaScript)2. | Browser cannot perform SRI digest checks on opaque responses, and extension scripts cannot inspect bytes2. | Classify content-inspection limits as OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT, except on Pinned Public Library CDNs where omitting crossorigin is TRUE\_DEFECT. |

## **3\. Violation Density and Blast-Radius Scoring Formula**

Binary rule scoring and rigid critical caps collapse scores disproportionately on large DOMs. Google Lighthouse scores Accessibility via Score \= (Sum of passed audit weights / Sum of applicable scored audit weights) \* 100, awarding zero partial credit per audit15. On an enterprise product grid of 300 thumbnails, 2 missing alt attributes fail the weight-10 image-alt audit completely39—and layering a rigid "1 critical failure \= cap score at 49 or 27" policy causes a 99%-accessible catalog to plummet unfairly. Conversely, pure unweighted failure ratios create blind spots: 1 unlabeled primary checkout button inside a 400-node DOM represents a 0.25% raw failure rate yet completely blocks transactions.  
To preserve proportionality while protecting critical journeys—borrowing Marker.io's per-issue incremental credit philosophy40 and Snyk's impact-plus-reachability prioritization41—the ScoringEngine implements a three-stage continuous model5.  
First, every evaluated node or resource ![][image11] for rule ![][image12] receives an **Interactive Blast Radius** weight ![][image13] assigned from DOM role, landmark context, and interactive affordance:

> 1. **Decorative / Repeating Listing Media (![][image14])**: Product catalog thumbnails, repeating carousel slides, spacer graphics, or non-interactive decorative badges.  
> 2. **Static Informational Content (![][image15])**: Article body copy, hero imagery, structural headings, and non-interactive landmarks.  
> 3. **Standard Interactive Controls (![][image16])**: Navigation links, filter checkboxes, tabs, dropdowns, and secondary action buttons.  
> 4. **Essential Flow & Transaction Controls (![][image17], ![][image18])**: Primary \<form\> submit buttons, authentication inputs, checkout/payment triggers, and modal escape controls.

Second, for any rule ![][image12] with failing subset ![][image19], the engine computes **Blast-Weighted Violation Density** (![][image20]) and combines a concave density term with a peak-blast-modulated exponential safeguard to obtain **Continuous Violation Pressure** (![][image21])5:  
![][image22]  
![][image23]  
Here ![][image24] (or 0 if ![][image25]), with calibrated starting constants ![][image26], ![][image27], ![][image28], and ![][image18]5. Using ![][image29] surfaces early regressions smoothly without sudden cliffs, while multiplying ![][image30] by ![][image31] inside the exponential term ensures two decorative thumbnails (![][image32]) do not trigger the same absolute-mass safeguard as two broken checkout buttons (![][image33])5. Page-level singleton rules (such as document language or login-page HSTS) naturally yield ![][image34] without special cases.  
Third, the category score ![][image35] aggregates across the scored rule set ![][image36] (PASS, TRUE\_DEFECT, and SYNTHETIC\_NOISE, excluding ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN and OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT) using base impact weights ![][image37] (Critical \= 10, Serious \= 7, Moderate \= 3, Minor \= 18), the corroborator's reality multiplier ![][image38], and a bounded single-rule hazard factor ![][image39] (![][image40])5:

## **4\. Centralized Extension Pipeline Architecture and TypeScript Model**

Implementing this triage pipeline inside a Manifest V3 browser extension requires strict alignment with Chrome's execution worlds, network observation limits, and service worker lifecycle44. Placing corroboration in page-injected scripts fails because page JavaScript can inspect or interfere with MAIN-world globals45 and cannot access HTTP headers, whereas relying on chrome.debugger in a store-distributed extension triggers sweeping install warnings and locks out Chrome DevTools3.

### **Extension Execution Topology and Manifest V3 Boundaries**

The optimal topology distributes lightweight raw collectors across execution worlds while centralizing ContextCorroborator and ScoringEngine inside the **MV3 Background Service Worker**.

| Extension Component | Chrome / MV3 APIs Used | Telemetry Collected | Hard Platform Limits and Risks | Architectural Role |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| MAIN World Probe | chrome.scripting.executeScript({ world: 'MAIN' })45 | PerformanceObserver (FCP, LCP, CLS, INP, LoAF scripts), PerformanceResourceTiming (renderBlockingStatus)1. | No access to chrome.\* extension APIs; page scripts can detect or modify MAIN-world logic45; LoAF omits cross-origin iframe attribution22. | Read-only performance and runtime capability sampler; dispatches snapshots to the ISOLATED content script. |
| ISOLATED Content Script | Default content-script environment (document\_idle / document\_end) | DOM tree, axe-core rule results, form/payment surface cues, \<link rel="canonical"\>, script tags and integrity attributes. | Blocked from cross-origin CSSOM inspection and no-cors opaque response headers/bodies2; cannot inspect raw HTTP headers. | Executes simple DOM FindingBuilder rules and sends normalized RawModuleData to the background worker. |
| MV3 Background Service Worker | Passive chrome.webRequest (onBeforeSendHeaders, onHeadersReceived, onCompleted with \['responseHeaders', 'extraHeaders'\]) \+ host\_permissions44 | HTTP status codes, redirect chains, CSP, HSTS, Timing-Allow-Origin, Set-Cookie, Link canonical headers. | Terminates after 30 s idle (5 min max request, 30 s fetch timeout), wiping globals—must persist state in chrome.storage (session/local) or IndexedDB (Web Storage unavailable)46; cannot read response bodies3; webRequestBlocking restricted to policy installs44. | Hosts ContextCorroborator, ScoringEngine, HSTS preload index, and report assembler. |
| Optional Pro / Enterprise CDP Collector | chrome.debugger (Network.enable, Network.getResponseBody)4 | Raw HTTP response bodies and full CDP network trees4; requires Network.enable active prior to completion to avoid "no resource with given identifier found" errors51. | Declaring debugger cannot be optional, triggers "Read and change all your data on all websites", shows a persistent debugging infobar (auto-closing 5 s post-detach), and locks out user DevTools3. | Strictly gated behind an opt-in enterprise/developer build; standard builds classify body-dependent checks as OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT3. |

Note two critical MV3 implementation details. First, declarativeNetRequest replaces blocking callbacks with declarative rule matching (block, redirect, modifyHeaders) and cannot be used to read response headers passively47; passive observation continues to rely on non-blocking chrome.webRequest with host\_permissions and 'extraHeaders' (required from Chrome 72+ to expose request headers such as Cookie, Referer, Accept-Language, and Accept-Encoding)44. Second, because MV3 service workers terminate after 30 seconds of inactivity46, incoming webRequest header records must flush incrementally into chrome.storage.session or IndexedDB keyed by (tabId, navigationId) rather than residing solely in in-memory variables46.

### **Decoupled Corroboration Middleware and TypeScript Contracts**

To ensure rule authors never embed domain-specific workarounds, rules implement a minimal FindingBuilder contract that inspects a single slice of RawModuleData, declares permission or timing prerequisites, and tags candidate findings for central cross-validation. The ContextCorroborator then executes ordered CorroborationPolicy middleware modules across the unified context snapshot, mutating reality states, adjusting ![][image38], and recording an auditable CorroborationTrace before handing off to ScoringEngine and UserReport.

TypeScript  
export type RealityState \=  
  \| 'TRUE\_DEFECT'  
  \| 'ARCHITECTURAL\_PATTERN'  
  \| 'OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT'  
  \| 'SYNTHETIC\_NOISE';

export type AuditCategory \= 'performance' \| 'security' \| 'accessibility' \| 'seo';

export type BlastTier \= 'decorative' \| 'content' \| 'interactive' \| 'critical\_flow';

export interface NodeBlastDescriptor {  
  selector: string;  
  tier: BlastTier;  
  /\*\* Numeric weight: decorative=0.25, content=1.0, interactive=1.5, critical\_flow=3.0 \*/  
  blastWeight: number;  
  failed: boolean;  
}

export interface RawModuleData {  
  tabId: number;  
  navigationId: string;  
  url: string;  
  collectedAtMs: number;  
  cwv: {  
    fcpMs: number \| null;  
    lcpMs: number \| null;  
    cls: number \| null;  
    inpMs: number \| null;  
    startedInBackgroundTab: boolean;  
    loafEntries: Array\<{ durationMs: number; scriptUrls: string\[\] }\>;  
  };  
  network: {  
    mainDocumentStatus: number;  
    redirectChain: string\[\];  
    responseHeaders: Record\<string, string\>;  
    cookies: Array\<{ name: string; domain: string; httpOnly: boolean; secure: boolean }\>;  
    resources: Array\<{  
      url: string;  
      initiatorType: string;  
      renderBlockingStatus?: 'blocking' \| 'non-blocking';  
      timingAllowOriginGranted: boolean;  
      isOpaqueNoCors: boolean;  
    }\>;  
    hasCdpBodyAccess: boolean;  
  };  
  surface: {  
    hasPasswordInput: boolean;  
    hasPaymentMount: boolean;  
    hasAuthenticatedSessionCookie: boolean;  
    hasStateChangingPostForm: boolean;  
    isolatedCheckoutOrigins: string\[\];  
    blockedCssomOrigins: string\[\];  
  };  
  seo: {  
    htmlCanonicals: string\[\];  
    httpLinkCanonicals: string\[\];  
    hreflangAlternates: Array\<{ lang: string; href: string }\>;  
  };  
}

export interface RawCandidateFinding {  
  ruleId: string;  
  category: AuditCategory;  
  /\*\* Base impact weight: 10 (Critical), 7 (Serious), 3 (Moderate), 1 (Minor) \*/  
  baseWeight: number;  
  applicable: boolean;  
  nodes: NodeBlastDescriptor\[\];  
  requiresPermissions?: {  
    crossOriginCssom?: boolean;  
    responseBody?: boolean;  
    timingAllowOriginForUrl?: string;  
  };  
  corroborationTags: Array\<  
    \| 'cwv-render-blocking'  
    \| 'cwv-main-thread'  
    \| 'security-header'  
    \| 'cookie-httponly'  
    \| 'sri-integrity'  
    \| 'seo-canonical'  
  \>;  
  metadata: Record\<string, unknown\>;  
}

export interface CorroborationTrace {  
  policyId: string;  
  previousState: RealityState;  
  nextState: RealityState;  
  multiplierApplied: number;  
  reason: string;  
}

export interface CorroboratedFinding extends RawCandidateFinding {  
  realityState: RealityState;  
  /\*\* Reality confidence multiplier in \[0, 1\] \*/  
  realityMultiplier: number;  
  /\*\* Blast-radius-weighted violation density in \[0, 1\] \*/  
  weightedDensity: number;  
  /\*\* Continuous violation pressure P\_r in \[0, 1\] \*/  
  violationPressure: number;  
  traces: CorroborationTrace\[\];  
}

export interface FindingBuilder {  
  readonly ruleId: string;  
  readonly category: AuditCategory;  
  evaluate(raw: RawModuleData): RawCandidateFinding;  
}

export interface CorroborationPolicy {  
  readonly policyId: string;  
  appliesTo(finding: RawCandidateFinding): boolean;  
  corroborate(  
    finding: CorroboratedFinding,  
    raw: RawModuleData  
  ): CorroboratedFinding;  
}

export interface CategoryScoreResult {  
  category: AuditCategory;  
  score: number;  
  telemetryCoverageIndex: number;  
  countsByState: Record\<RealityState \| 'PASS', number\>;  
}

export interface UserReport {  
  url: string;  
  navigationId: string;  
  generatedAtMs: number;  
  categories: Record\<AuditCategory, CategoryScoreResult\>;  
  actionableDefects: CorroboratedFinding\[\];  
  architecturalPatterns: CorroboratedFinding\[\];  
  observabilityLimits: CorroboratedFinding\[\];  
  suppressedNoise: CorroboratedFinding\[\];  
}

export interface AuditPipeline {  
  buildFindings(raw: RawModuleData, builders: FindingBuilder\[\]): RawCandidateFinding\[\];  
  corroborate(  
    candidates: RawCandidateFinding\[\],  
    raw: RawModuleData,  
    policies: CorroborationPolicy\[\]  
  ): CorroboratedFinding\[\];  
  score(findings: CorroboratedFinding\[\]): Record\<AuditCategory, CategoryScoreResult\>;  
  assembleReport(  
    raw: RawModuleData,  
    findings: CorroboratedFinding\[\],  
    categories: Record\<AuditCategory, CategoryScoreResult\>  
  ): UserReport;  
}

In execution order, buildFindings turns raw collector snapshots into atomic candidates; corroborate seeds failing candidates at TRUE\_DEFECT (![][image2]) and applies policies in strict precedence (ObservabilityBarrierPolicy \-\> AssetMutabilityPolicy \-\> CanonicalSemanticsPolicy \-\> SurfaceCapabilityPolicy \-\> CwvRealityGatePolicy); score calculates ![][image53], ![][image54], and TCI; and assembleReport separates verified defects from enterprise patterns, visibility gaps, and suppressed diagnostics so users retain full audit traceability without score distortion.

## **5\. Industry Patterns for False-Positive Suppression and Triage**

Production auditing, security, and observability platforms converge on a core lesson: raw rule engines lose engineering credibility unless paired with explicit uncertainty states, runtime reachability/corroboration, and impact-weighted prioritization. Comparing six established platforms highlights how each manages enterprise noise and where remaining gaps motivate the pipeline above.

| Platform | Primary Denoising / Triage Mechanism | Granularity & Uncertainty Handling | Documented Gaps or Trade-Offs | Architectural Lesson Adopted |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Google Lighthouse | scoreDisplayMode separation; field-calibrated scoring curves9. | Isolates notApplicable and informative checks from scores9; Lighthouse 10 weights TBT (30%), LCP (25%), CLS (25%), FCP (10%), Speed Index (10%)43. | Lantern simulation can misflag module scripts as render-blocking despite fast observed FCP16; accessibility audits remain binary pass/fail15. | Exclude non-applicable audits from denominators and let observed CWV override simulated heuristics9. |
| Deque axe-core & Axe DevTools Pro | Zero-false-positive bias via incomplete (cantTell) state \+ Intelligent Guided Tests (IGT)6. | Refuses to guess on ambiguous checks (e.g., contrast over images, missing frame instrumentation), placing them in incomplete40; AI Interactive Elements IGT explains "Why AI made this recommendation"58. | Automated rules catch an estimated 57% of issues by volume per Deque's own report (\~30–40% of WCAG criteria), requiring IGT or manual checks to claim 80%+ coverage per Deque's webinar summaries8. | Route unprovable cross-origin or styling checks into an explicit non-penalizing OBSERVABILITY\_LIMIT state56. |
| Snyk | Reachability Analysis \+ continuous 0–1,000 Risk and Priority Scores41. | Separates urgency rankings (0–1,000) from severity bands; Risk Score multiplies Impact and Likelihood incorporating EPSS, exploit maturity, reachability, and application context41. | Competitor evaluations (Semgrep) contend that without reachability analysis enabled, Snyk scans can still overwhelm teams with static alert volume60. | Make contextual reachability (Surface Capability and runtime execution) mandatory in middleware rather than optional42. |
| Datadog RUM | Frustration Signals \+ p75 CWV element selectors \+ collection guards23. | Captures Rage Clicks (\>3 clicks in a 1 s sliding window), Dead Clicks, and Error Clicks62; drops FCP/LCP on background-opened tabs and omits INP when zero interactions occur23. | Requires live production traffic rather than single-tab passive auditing; cross-origin LoAF/timing limits still apply22. | Discard background-tab paint metrics and scale findings by interactive element blast radius23. |
| Sentry (and Error Trackers) | Inbound default noise filters (ignoreErrors, denyUrls)64. | Strips known browser/cross-origin noise ("Script error.", "ResizeObserver loop limit exceeded") before alerting, as documented in ecosystem references64. | Over-broad static string filters can conceal genuine defects unless provenance is retained. | Suppress benign synthetic artifacts centrally while preserving traceable records in suppressedNoise64. |
| OWASP ZAP (Passive Rules) | Orthogonal Alert Threshold (Low/Medium/High) and Confidence (Low/Medium/High)11. | Ignores missing CSP headers on redirects unless Low threshold is active; ignores underscore strings in PII rules at Medium/High thresholds; reduces Cache-Control findings to Info11. | Threshold tuning is largely global per scan policy rather than dynamically adapting to page DOM capability. | Separate confidence (![][image38]) from structural severity (![][image37]) and gate passive header checks on HTTP redirect/response context11. |

Synthesizing these practices clarifies why naive browser audit extensions burn developer trust: they inherit strict rule libraries without building the corroboration layer that keeps Lighthouse, Deque, Snyk, Datadog, and OWASP ZAP actionable on complex architectures. By grounding raw rules in an MV3 ContextCorroborator backed by live Core Web Vitals, DOM surface capability profiles, canonical superset logic, SRI mutability rules, and blast-radius-weighted scoring, your extension turns noisy enterprise edge cases into transparent, trustworthy intelligence.
